10.1021_acsenergylett.6c01307: The complex crystallization of solution-processed polycrystalline perovskite films leads to the formation of deep-trap states, ultimately hindering the performance of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, we have devised a facile and practical solvent polishing (SP) approach utilizing a sulfolane and chlorobenzene mixture to reconstruct the surface of triple-cation perovskite films. This strategy enables the removal of the surface-oriented phases containing trap sites, exposing compact vertically aligned crystalline domains with lower defectiveness and lower surface roughness, ultimately leading to enhanced carrier transport, facilitating interfacial charge extraction, and suppressing nonradiative recombination losses. Consequently, the PSCs fabricated with SP exhibit a higher power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 22.0% with a remarkable fill factor (FF) of 82%, surpassing the control device (20.5% PCE and 79% FF). Additionally, the SP-treated devices retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 40 days at 40% relative humidity, indicating improved shelf stability under moderately humid conditions.
10.1038_s41467-026-74735-0: Nanofluidic ion gating underpins both biological signal transduction and iontronic signal processing. However, a simple and reliable mechanism that functions independently of local electrochemical conditions remains unavailable, hindering interference-free integration of artificial iontronic components with biological counterparts. Here, we present a nanofluidic device that enabled ionic gating through pervaporation-driven precipitation and rehydration-driven dissolution (PP&RD) of salt solutions within a nanochannel. Pervaporation induced local salt precipitation in the nanochannel, forming an electrical blockage that suppressed conductance (OFF state), whereas rehydration dissolved the precipitate and restored the conductance (ON state). The ionic gating device exhibited an ON–OFF conductance ratio exceeding 100, fully reversible operation performance, and robust switching across experimental conditions. By integrating two ionic gates in parallel or in series within a single device, we further implement Boolean OR and AND logic operations. PP&RD-based ionic gating thus provided a simple, versatile, and practical foundation for scalable iontronic circuit architecture. Nanofluidic ion gating is crucial for advancing artificial iontronic technologies that can seamlessly integrate with biological systems, yet existing methods often rely on local electrochemical conditions, limiting their scalability and functionality. This study introduces an ionic gating mechanism based on pervaporation-driven precipitation and rehydration-driven dissolution, achieving a high ON–OFF conductance ratio.
